summary:
• **Temperature Definition**: Temperature is the measure of the degree of hotness or coldness of an object. It helps us determine how hot or cold a substance is quantitatively.
• **Measurement Device**: Temperature is measured using a device called a **thermometer**.
• **Clinical Thermometer**: This is specifically designed to measure human body temperature. The normal human body temperature is **37°C** (or 98.6°F). It has a **kink** (narrow constriction) near the bulb that prevents the mercury level from falling on its own, allowing us to read the temperature accurately after removing it from the mouth.
• **Laboratory Thermometer**: Used to measure temperatures of substances in a laboratory. It does not have a kink, so its temperature must be read while it is still in contact with the substance being measured.
• **Units of Temperature**: The most common units are **degree Celsius (°C)** and **degree Fahrenheit (°F)**. The SI unit of temperature is **Kelvin (K)**.
